notes: PROJECTION registry (§0.9/§0.18). The flagship page public/site/agentic-governance-lifecycle.html renders FROM this file.

Non-collision with kye.lifecycle.v1: that registry owns generalised STATE MACHINES (ordered states); authority-lifecycle.html owns the on-the-wire signed-state sequence. This spine is the CONCERN-LEVEL map binding each governance concern to its existing canonical page + schema + engine. No state-machine is redefined here.

§0.16 boundary verbs are non-negotiable at the integration boundary: Contestability ENABLES (KYE provides Evidence Pack + Replay Proof substrate; it does NOT adjudicate disputes), Renewal/Revocation EMITS (the enforcement rail acts on a KYE-decided revocation). These mirror internal anti_dilution_clauses kye:anti-dilution:not-dispute and kye:anti-dilution:not-payment-rail.

Contestability is the only stage whose canonical content surface is this flagship page (orphan concept resolved per §0.12 — registered in internal as agentic-governance-lifecycle-contestability). Every other stage links to a pre-existing canonical surface.

stages.name: Intent
stages.summary: A principal declares a purpose-scoped intent before any action. KYE binds the intent to a Purpose Permission grant so the act inherits a standing rule, not an ad-hoc allowance.

stages.name: Action Admissibility
stages.summary: Before any authority or formal-rule check runs, KYE decides whether the proposed action is admissible into the authority pipeline at all — six decision values, one canonical gate.

stages.name: Authority Resolution
stages.summary: KYE resolves the chain of authority behind the act — which grant, from which principal, attenuated through which delegation — to a single authoritative answer at the point of action.

stages.name: Delegation and Scope
stages.summary: KYE attenuates authority down the delegation chain and pins the scope each hop may spend. An agent cannot exceed the scope its delegation envelope grants.

stages.name: Execution Control
stages.summary: At the gateway, KYE issues the verdict that admits or denies the action and records the Decision Map that links inputs to outcome — the runtime control point the act passes through.

stages.name: Evidence Pack
stages.summary: KYE seals the signed, replayable Evidence Pack — audit-chain entries, Decision Maps, signatures and the public-key set an auditor verifies offline from public keys alone.

stages.name: Authority Finality
stages.summary: KYE resolves the act to finality — a sealed, signed, non-repudiable end state. Every act has authority; every authority has finality. This is the property KYE owns end-to-end.

stages.name: Reality Coupling
stages.summary: KYE detects stable drift — when a still-locally-valid authority has decoupled from the reality it was granted against — and decides whether the act must be revalidated against fresh ground truth.

stages.name: Contestability
stages.summary: KYE ENABLES contestability by providing the Evidence Pack and Replay Proof substrate any third party re-derives from public keys alone. KYE is not a dispute-resolution adjudicator — it makes the contest evidentiary, not opinion.

stages.name: Renewal and Revocation
stages.summary: KYE decides and EMITS the revocation; the enforcement rail acts on it. Revocations propagate recursively down delegation chains and expiries trigger automatic state transitions after finality.
